title: Highly nonlinear Moiré exciton and trion polaritons
authors: Arnab Barman Ray, Trevor Ollis, Fei Cheng, Adam L. Freidman, Aubrey T. Hanbicki, Anthony Nickolas Vamivakas
abstract: Moiré multi-layers of transition metal dichalcogenides have been shown to exhibit optical responses that are endowed with a richness that is absent in single monolayers. Much of this can be attributed to the Moiré superlattice that modulates the electronic landscape of these heterostructures. Strongly coupled layer-hybridized excitons in MoSe2/WS2 heterobilayers have been shown to exhibit enhanced optical nonlinearities. In this work we strongly couple layer hybridized excitons and trions in n-doped $\text{MoSe}_2 / \text{WS}_2$ heterobilayers inside an optical microcavity. We find that the additional Lindhard screening from dopant electrons and the formation of trions result in a strikingly non-monotonic nonlinear response. The absence of electron capture in the Moiré superlattice plays a crucial role, promising very large second-order nonlinearities. In this work, trion polaritons manifest as high velocity hot polaritons, reaching nominal diffusion lengths approaching 100 microns.
summary: This paper reports on the observation of strongly coupled Moiré exciton and trion polaritons in semiconductor heterobilayers within an optical microcavity. By combining theory and experiment, the authors reveal a striking non-monotonic nonlinear response to excitation density. The findings highlight large group velocities and unprecedentedly large second-order nonlinearities controllable via doping.
main_problem: The study investigates the highly nonlinear optical response of strongly coupled Moiré exciton and trion polaritons in heterobilayers. A key focus is understanding the non-monotonic energy shifts and oscillator strength variations as a function of excitation density.
main_result: The research demonstrates that the system exhibits strong coupling, leading to lower polariton branches with non-monotonic energy shifts and exceptionally large second-order nonlinearities ($\sim 10^2 \mu	ext{m}$ diffusion length).
method: The work combines theoretical modeling using rate equations and Hamiltonian diagonalization with experimental optical measurements (PL spectroscopy) performed at cryogenic temperatures.
model_or_system: The physical system is an n-doped $	ext{MoSe}_2/	ext{WS}_2$ heterobilayer placed inside a metal-DBR microcavity. The model incorporates coupled exciton ($	ext{X}$) and trion ($	ext{X}^{-2}$) resonances, utilizing concepts like Lindhard screening to describe carrier interactions.
key_observables: Nonlinear dependence of oscillator strengths on polariton density; non-monotonic energy shift in the lower polariton branch; nominal diffusion length ($L_D$) for trion polaritons.
important_parameters: Cryogenic temperature (5 K); initial dopant electron concentration ($n_e$); coupling constants ($\Omega$); screening coefficients ($ eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes constant dephasing of 0D excitons when fixing the cavity resonance energy during density variation studies.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate device geometry, temperature-dependent PL spectra identifying exciton/trion resonances, and spatio-spectra showing extended diffusion tails near trion polariton energies.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical platform (heterobilayers in microcavities) to modeling the coupled dynamics using rate equations. It then analyzes density dependence via nonlinear shifts and concludes by quantifying large-scale spatial transport properties of the resulting polaritons.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it deals with cavity quantum electrodynamics (Cavity QED) in solid-state systems, specifically exploring strong light-matter coupling and nonlinear dynamics mediated by excitons/trions—a core topic in AMO physics and quantum optics.
